scenes: In twenty thirteen, Bitcoin split into two chains.
And developers chose to kill the newer one.
March eleventh, twenty thirteen. Bitcoin version zero point eight was brand new.
Then one huge block hit the network, with over five thousand transactions.
New nodes accepted it. Old nodes couldn't read it.
Their old database ran out of locks. Bitcoin split in two.
Mount Gox and Bit Pay paused deposits.
Developers picked the old chain. Big mining pools downgraded.
About six hours later, the chains joined again.
And someone double spent ten thousand dollars against Oh-Kay Pay.
